video_overlay_text_observed: A screen recording of another account's post, phone UI and caption bar included. Burned-in overlays: "THIS IS MASSIVE!! A CALIFORNIAN WOMAN...", "MORE FOOTAGE IN 8 / IT GETS CRAZY", "90 SECOND EXCERPT", "These are excerpts. See my page for full version.", and a persistent credit line "FOLLOW YOURNEWS.COM & ARIANA MASTERS". A FlightRadar24 screen is shown mid-clip with tail number N904DK, a Beech C90A King Air, in a loitering pattern over Sonora and Columbia, California at 194 knots.
audio_content_summary: A narrated package built around footage of a Tuolumne County resident confronting a pilot in the Modesto Jet Center at 1:30 a.m. after tracking his aircraft on FlightRadar24. The narrator says she has tracked flights for several years, collected over twenty rainwater samples and filed public-records requests showing elevated aluminium, barium, strontium, titanium and magnesium, and cites a separate effort that sampled air at altitude behind aircraft. On camera she tells the pilot residents are "tired of you dumping heavy metals all over our county," that every time he flies the samples come back high, and that legal action against his company is coming; she raises contaminated soil, aluminium-tolerant seed, and early-onset dementia. The pilot answers that he is not the person to bring it to, that the flights have run for thirty years and are public knowledge, and that it is "not illegal." She replies: "It's not illegal yet."
implied_frame:
Frames the flights as a covert heavy-metal spraying program that residents have caught in the act. The aircraft identification is correct and the program is real; the payload allegation is the part that is unestablished.

RECORDED (verified, see the evidence records): N904DK is a Beech C90A registered to a Fargo, North Dakota lessor at the same address as a cloud-seeding contractor, holding a restricted-category certificate whose approved operations include Weather Control. Turlock and Modesto Irrigation Districts have seeded the Tuolumne watershed by aircraft since 1990 using silver-iodide flares, reviewed under CEQA in 1989 with Tuolumne named as the affected county. Weather modification has been federally reportable since 1971 under Public Law 92-205, and California requires a notice of intention, publication in each affected county, notice to county supervisors, and a record of the agents used. The pilot's two factual assertions on camera — thirty years, and not illegal — are both correct.

NOT ADOPTED: that the rainwater samples show hazardous levels of aluminium, barium, strontium, titanium and magnesium. No laboratory report, concentration, unit, detection limit or control comparison has been produced in any source reachable here; the published collection method is open tubs, which is not a chain of custody. That absence is not a refutation — the samples may exist and may say what she says. It means the claim is unverified, and the site does not carry unverified lab findings as fact. Also not adopted: that those metals are what the aircraft release (the filings declare silver iodide and nothing else); the at-altitude air-sampling program described by the narrator, which names no laboratory and cites no report; that soil contamination has driven a market in aluminium-tolerant seed; and that the flights are causing early-onset dementia or Alzheimer's in the county.

CONTESTED, BOTH SIDES ON RECORD: whether Tuolumne County's board of supervisors received the notice California law requires. She says it did not. The districts' own February 2025 fact sheet says they have noticed "far beyond what is required." Neither has been confirmed here, and a county clerk's records would settle it.

GROUP C IS ZERO. Nothing in the clip is fabricated out of nothing — the aircraft, the operator, the program, the flight track and the confrontation are all real. The disputed material is interpretation and unverified measurement, which belongs in B.

video_download_status: Original pulled via yt-dlp (~12.9 MB); delivery ~13.7 MB webm.
notes: The pilot is a private individual and is not named in any reader-facing text; the transcript captures a first name, which stays here. The resident publishes under the handle MellowKat / @MellowKatRS and her own Substack; the confrontation is reported as 1 February 2025 at the Modesto Jet Center. This capture is a screen recording of a repost, credited on screen to yournews.com and Ariana Masters, itself excerpting a longer interview — three layers above the original footage. Whisper mangles several passages: "Tuolumne" as "to Lume" and "over to Lume County", "Beech C90 King Air" as "beach C-90 kink air", "seeding" as "seating", "barium" as "ferium", and the narrator's at-altitude sampling passage as "a NOAA slide lab with top side descendant." The strongest open thread is the § 411 notice question, which is documentary and answerable.
